solutions.check: 29 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Secure senior Tory extremist leaders in the cooler!

indicators.note: the leaders of the three words are their opening letters
the letters go inside the cooler

parts.note: first letters of Senior, Tory, Extremist

explanation.surface: A call to lock up a hard-right Conservative grandee in prison, 'the cooler' being slang for jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cooler' is slang for prison, which suits the surface, but here it is simply a device that cools.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain verb synonym, as when a seatbelt is done up to keep you secure.

clue.text: Paid player to introduce Conservative mail shot for broadcast

indicators.note: the paid player comes first and introduces what follows, so it leads the answer

parts.note: a pro is a professional, a player who is paid

indicators.note: a shot item is wrecked or ruined, so the letters of mail are scrambled

explanation.surface: A paid campaigner fronts a Tory leaflet drop sent out to voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mail shot' looks like a direct-mail campaign, but 'shot' scrambles MAIL into LAIM. PRO 'to introduce' C means the paid player goes first, then C, then LAIM.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim something is to announce it publicly, which is what broadcasting news does.

clue.text: Ramshackle hut getting in a state

indicators.note: the letter a gets into the scrambled hut, sitting inside it
a ramshackle building is falling apart, so the letters of hut are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tumbledown shack is found somewhere in one of America's states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ramshackle' turns HUT into UTH, and 'getting in' puts A inside it: UT-A-H.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty United States, in the American West.

clue.text: Being a puny sort, Sunak is doing a U-turn, taking time

indicators.note: turning back reverses the letters
the reversed letters take the time inside them

parts.note: Rishi Sunak was PM, prime minister; then IS
HR = hour, a unit of time

explanation.surface: A jibe that the prime minister, backtracking on a policy and taking his time, looks feeble.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a political U-turn; in the wordplay it is the letters of PM IS that turn round, to SIMP, before HR goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: a small, weedy person, named after the tiny crustacean.

clue.text: Following slimy creature, Farage's lead, set about creating a political fight

indicators.note: Farage's first letter comes after the slimy creature in the answer

parts.note: a slug is a slimy garden mollusc

indicators.note: a lead is what goes in front, so the first letter of Farage is taken

parts.note: Nigel Farage, the Reform UK politician, supplies his first letter

indicators.note: set about suggests the letters of set being knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Behind a slimy figure, Farage's lead sets the scene for a nasty political brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slimy creature' is a jibe in the surface but a plain garden mollusc in the wordplay; 'Following' and 'lead' bring in Farage's initial, and 'about' jumbles the three letters of set.
explanation.definitionFit: A slugfest is an informal word for a bruising contest, originally a boxing match full of heavy punches.

clue.text: Topless female only coarse to be of interest

definitions.note: ENGROSS is transitive, to hold someone's interest; the definition is loose

parts.note: HEN, a female bird, without its first letter

explanation.surface: A leering remark that a topless woman is merely crude titillation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless female' suggests a naked woman; it means HEN with its top letter lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: something absorbing holds your attention completely.

clue.text: Labour party faction wants leader's debut broadcast to be in short, easily assimilated segments

indicators.note: the letters are placed inside the segments

parts.note: bites, as in sound bites or bite-sized chunks

indicators.note: a leader's debut is the first letter of 'leader'

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A Labour faction wants its leader's first broadcast chopped into sound bites.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair was the New Labour prime minister, and the segments are sound bites, the short quotable lines politicians feed the media.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Tony Blair: the centrist New Labour wing that backed his line.

clue.text: Brown, as well as Tony, ultimately a follower of Napoleon?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown and Tony Blair cast as disciples of Napoleon.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown and Tony suggest the Labour prime ministers Gordon Brown and Tony Blair. Napoleon is a grade of cognac, so the spirit's name follows it on the label.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon brandy is a named grade of cognac, so the word follows Napoleon; the question mark flags the wordplay on 'follower'.

clue.text: County almost meets terrible end — Labour finally to resign?

indicators.note: almost the whole word, so the county loses its last letter

parts.note: Surrey is an English county south-west of London

indicators.note: something terrible is in a mess, so the letters of end are jumbled
finally points to the last letter of Labour

parts.note: the last letter of Labour is taken

explanation.surface: A shire nearly suffers a dreadful fate, and Labour finally throws in the towel.
explanation.walkthrough: SURREY 'almost' gives SURRE; 'terrible' rearranges END into NDE; 'finally' gives R from Labour.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to give up or yield, and to resign also means to give up a position or contest.

clue.text: Brothel encouraged accommodating beauty

indicators.note: the words accommodate, hold, the answer inside them

parts.note: the answer spans the end of 'Brothel' and the start of 'encouraged'

explanation.surface: A brothel was keen to take on a pretty girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The legendary beauty of Troy, whose face 'launched a thousand ships', sits across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Helen of Troy, the figure of Greek legend who stands for beauty itself.

clue.text: Bill grabs tit roughly (very top area)

indicators.note: the bill takes hold of the other letters and holds them inside it

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: roughly means not exactly, so the letters of tit are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Bill crudely lunges at a small bird, or at something ruder.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill is not a man's name but an account; 'grabs' and 'roughly' work on the bird, and the parenthesis is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the room right at the top of a house, under the roof.

clue.text: Sign of what's to come of cleaner about to leave non-stop boozer?

parts.note: CHAR, a cleaner, without C (circa, about)

explanation.surface: A cleaner is about to walk out on an employer who never stops drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a cleaning lady; C is short for circa, about.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym; the word first meant a herald sent ahead to announce an arrival.

clue.text: Fashion deals in rejections

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: The fashion trade deals in knock-backs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like the subject of the sentence, the clothing trade; it is the instruction to reshape DEALS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, plural to match: refusals of a claim or request.

clue.text: Go easy on the feeling, stupid!

parts.note: going easy on something means using less of it

explanation.surface: A plea to tone down the emotion, with an insult attached.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the instruction literally: use less of the feeling, SENSE LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: lacking good sense, as in a pointless, foolish act.

clue.text: Who ruled those common people with iron

definitions.note: the definition is a relative clause, 'one who ruled', standing for a noun

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: A question of who governed the masses with an iron fist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' suggests an iron rule; it is the household chore, to press.
explanation.definitionFit: A female monarch of an empire; the relative clause stands for the ruler herself.

clue.text: In which, routine Sunak opening argument is made?

definitions.text: In which, routine Sunak opening argument is made?

indicators.note: a word's opening is its first letter

explanation.surface: Where the prime minister routinely opens the argument.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: the Commons is Parliament's lower house, where Sunak as prime minister routinely made his case.
explanation.definitionFit: Read straight, the whole clue describes a sitting of the House of Commons, the chamber where the prime minister argues his case.

clue.text: Dicky sat on stopper — criminal!

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first part sits on top of the second

explanation.surface: Someone sat on a plug and got called a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky is British slang for weak or unwell, as in a dicky heart; off means the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for someone who breaks the law.

clue.text: In USA Bill's crafty token ban

indicators.note: crafty suggests cunningly worked, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An American politician called Bill slyly bans a token.
explanation.walkthrough: The ''s' stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional use: Americans say bill for what Britons call a note.

clue.text: A green old leader

definitions.meaning: a shade of green named after an English city, worn by Robin Hood
the US president who led the Union through the Civil War

explanation.surface: An environmentalist politician of an earlier generation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' suggests an environmentalist; Lincoln green is a traditional cloth colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: a shade of green named after the English city, and Abraham, the 16th US president.

clue.text: Pressing your lower half against a bloke

parts.note: a gent is a man, a bloke

explanation.surface: Rubbing one's crotch up against a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower half' sounds like the body below the waist; it is the latter half of the word YOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain adjective synonym, as in a pressing need.

clue.text: Aggravate fashionable female with male shit

indicators.note: something shit is rubbish or broken, so the letters of male are scrambled

explanation.surface: A trendy woman with a lousy man is bound to stir up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: IN and F, then 'shit' rearranges MALE into LAME.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflame a situation is to make it worse or more heated, which is what aggravating does.

clue.text: Get off with a blonde?

explanation.surface: Pulling a blonde, in the British slang sense of getting off with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to 'get off with' someone is to kiss or pull them; the definition is only 'Get off', as from a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym for leaving a vehicle, as passengers do from a bus.

clue.text: Knock down, applying bolt to balls

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls

explanation.surface: A violent instruction to strike someone in the testicles.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls bowled from one end in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: what a car does when it hits a pedestrian.

clue.text: A sign one enters for Amazon?

indicators.note: A enters, goes inside, the sign

parts.note: Virgo, one sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A sign that a buyer has signed up to Amazon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazon' suggests the online shop; here it is a warrior woman of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: An Amazon was a warrior woman of Greek myth, and the answer means a fierce, domineering woman.

clue.text: Australia is able to control a leak?

definitions.meaning: one of the seven great landmasses of the world
the medical word for having control of the bladder

explanation.surface: A claim that the whole of Australia can hold its water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leak' is slang for urinating, which gives the medical sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: Australia is the smallest of the seven great landmasses, and the medical sense means having bladder control.

clue.text: Bird's outside with plonker

indicators.note: the bird goes outside the letter

parts.note: a tit is a small bird; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A woman is out with an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is British slang for a woman, but here it is the small bird. A plonker is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym; plonker is British slang for a fool.

clue.text: Hardliner very full of gall

indicators.note: the words are full of the answer, holding it inside

parts.note: the answer spans the last three letters of 'Hardliner' and the first two of 'very'

explanation.surface: A hardliner with a great deal of cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardliner' pulls towards politics, but only its tail counts, run together with the start of 'very'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the sense of cheek or effrontery, as in 'the gall of it'.

clue.text: One who sponges Spike before church?

parts.note: Spike Lee, the American film director

explanation.surface: A question about who gets a spiked drink before the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' looks like a verb or a spike; it is the first name of the director Spike Lee.
explanation.definitionFit: Metaphor: the worm clings and draws blood, as a sponger draws money from others.

clue.text: Society family, pissed and very clinging

explanation.surface: A posh family is drunk and very clingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed' is British slang for drunk, not angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: clothes that fit like a second skin cling very closely.
